title: Another
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In 1998 Koichi Sakakibara transfers to Class 3-3 at Yomiyama North Middle School, where classmates act as if the aloof, eyepatched Mei Misaki does not exist. Since a student's death 26 years earlier, an extra 'dead' person joins the class in some years and students and their relatives die in accidents. Koichi tries to uncover how the curse works before it claims him.
life_message: Facing a hard truth together, rather than denying it or scapegoating one person, is what finally breaks a cycle of grief and death.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflict is with a curse, not personal insult.

Order vs freedom.evidence: The class enforces strict unwritten rules to survive.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty is to the class as a whole; family members also die.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Class officers and teachers set countermeasures others must follow.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Inherited rituals guide the class, though Koichi reasons through them.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival of the class drives every choice.

folkways.japan: The class's collective silence and shunning reflect Japanese group-harmony pressures and the practice of reading the air, examined critically.

delivery.evidence: No source comments on delivery; summaries show the outlook carried by plot and character choices (to verify).
delivery.note: Its warning about scapegoating and denial is carried by the mystery's plot as Koichi uncovers how the curse works.

winners_losers: Koichi and Mei uncover the truth and survive; many classmates and relatives die. Sympathy goes to honesty and to the outcast.
